content: The strategic hubs and corridors that dominated bulk transport activities between 2020 and 2023 laid the foundational infrastructure for the current market landscape. Major Bulk Freight Transport Routes and Regional Focus (2020-2023) Region Strategic Focus Time Period Asia-Pacific Strategic hubs and corridors 2020-2023 Europe Strategic hubs and corridors 2020-2023 Data Source: Google Search Fleet Capacities and Specializations The global bulk freight vessel landscape is characterized by a diverse array of vessel types tailored to transport dry bulk commodities, forming the critical backbone of the maritime logistics industry. The primary categories utilized within this sector include Handysize, Handymax or Supramax, Panamax, Capesize, and Very Large Ore Carriers (VLOCs) [18] . Each of these vessel classifications is defined by its distinct carrying capacity and its suitability for specific types of cargo, enabling fleet operators to cater to a wide spectrum of global trade requirements. The commodities predominantly handled by these fleets include essential raw materials and goods such as iron ore, coal, cement, bauxite, and various agricultural products [18] . By leveraging a combination of these vessel types, freight companies can optimize their operational networks to address the varying demands of international supply chains. Understanding the distinct operational profiles of these vessels is essential for competitive and market intelligence, as fleet composition directly dictates a carrier's ability to respond to shifting global commodity demands. Fleet specialization is largely driven by the physical dimensions of the vessels and the infrastructural constraints of destination ports. Handysize vessels, which typically feature a carrying capacity ranging from 10,000 to 40,000 Deadweight Tonnage (DWT), are highly regarded for their operational versatility [5] . Their relatively smaller size allows them to access a wider variety of smaller, less developed ports, making them indispensable for regional distribution and specialized cargo missions where draft restrictions prevent the entry of larger ships. Conversely, Capesize vessels are designed to accommodate massive shipments exceeding 80,000 DWT [5] . These highly specialized vessels operate predominantly on fixed, deep-water routes and are dedicated to the transport of high-volume industrial materials, most notably coal and iron ore [5] .
